title: Cell Biology
description: Organelles, membranes and cell division: the cell chapter for Class 11-12 and first-year biology.

cards.question: Who proposed the cell theory?
cards.answer: Matthias Schleiden (plants, 1838) and Theodor Schwann (animals, 1839).

cards.question: What did Rudolf Virchow add to the cell theory?
cards.answer: That all cells arise from pre-existing cells: "Omnis cellula e cellula" (1855).

cards.question: Who first saw and named cells?
cards.answer: Robert Hooke, in 1665, while looking at thin slices of cork.

cards.question: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell, and why?
cards.answer: Mitochondria. They make most of the cell's ATP through aerobic respiration.

cards.question: Why are mitochondria and chloroplasts called semi-autonomous?
cards.answer: They have their own DNA and 70S ribosomes, so they can make some of their own proteins.

cards.question: What is the function of ribosomes?
cards.answer: Protein synthesis: they translate mRNA into a chain of amino acids.

cards.question: Which type of ribosome is found in prokaryotes, and which in the eukaryotic cytoplasm?
cards.answer: Prokaryotes: 70S (50S + 30S subunits). Eukaryotic cytoplasm: 80S (60S + 40S subunits).

cards.question: How is rough ER different from smooth ER?
cards.answer: Rough ER has ribosomes on it and makes proteins for secretion and membranes. Smooth ER has no ribosomes; it makes lipids such as steroids and helps in detoxification.

cards.question: What does the Golgi apparatus do?
cards.answer: It modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles for secretion or delivery. Glycoproteins and glycolipids are formed here.

cards.question: Why are lysosomes called suicide bags?
cards.answer: They hold hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes. If the lysosome bursts, these enzymes can digest the cell itself.

cards.question: What is the function of the nucleolus?
cards.answer: It is the site where rRNA is made and ribosome subunits are assembled.

cards.question: What is the membrane around the plant vacuole called?
cards.answer: The tonoplast.

cards.question: Name structures found in plant cells but not in animal cells.
cards.answer: Cell wall, plastids such as chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole.

cards.question: Which cell structure is present in animal cells but absent in most higher plant cells?
cards.answer: Centrioles.

cards.question: Who proposed the fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane?
cards.answer: Singer and Nicolson, in 1972. The membrane is a fluid lipid bilayer with proteins floating in it.

cards.question: What is the main lipid in the plasma membrane and how is it arranged?
cards.answer: Phospholipids, in a bilayer: water-loving heads face outward and water-fearing tails face inward.

cards.question: What is osmosis?
cards.answer: Movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration.

cards.question: How is active transport different from passive transport?
cards.answer: Active transport uses energy (ATP) to move substances against their concentration gradient, as in the Na+/K+ pump. Passive transport needs no energy and moves down the gradient.

cards.question: What is the cell wall made of in plants, fungi and bacteria?
cards.answer: Plants: cellulose. Fungi: chitin. Bacteria: peptidoglycan.

cards.question: What is the key difference between a prokaryotic and a eukaryotic cell?
cards.answer: Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound nucleus or membrane-bound organelles; their DNA lies in a region called the nucleoid.

cards.question: List the phases of mitosis in order.
cards.answer: Prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, followed by cytokinesis.

cards.question: In which phase of interphase does DNA replicate?
cards.answer: S phase (synthesis phase).

cards.question: In which stage of mitosis do chromosomes line up at the equator of the cell?
cards.answer: Metaphase. The chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate.

cards.question: What is the main result of meiosis?
cards.answer: Four haploid cells with half the chromosome number of the parent cell. Crossing over and independent assortment create variation.

cards.question: In which stage of meiosis does crossing over happen?
cards.answer: Pachytene, in prophase I.
